Commentary.Commentary: That ends the first game of this 5-match ODI series. Perhaps, had Australia won with say, 4 or 5 wickets to spare, we might have said that it was a convincing victory. But this collapse towards the end tells us that there is a lot of action to come in the coming 4 games. Do join us for the second ODI on Wednesday, 24th August, 2016 at 1430 IST (0900 GMT). Until then, Adios! Take Care!

Winning captain, STEVEN SMITH says it's always nice to be on this side of the result. Accepts they had a tough time in the Tests and is happy to come up with something like this. Further says his team did well to bat on a wicket which wasn't at all easy. Appreciates the way his bowlers brought them back in the game and restricting Sri Lanka to a total that was in their grasp. Informs that they had certain plans to deal with this Lankan side and that it paid off here tonight.

Sri Lankan skipper ANGELO MATHEWS says that his side was 20-30 runs short. It was not an easy wicket to bat on, he says and credits Chandimal and Mendis for their innings. Feels that Dilruwan Perera, Milinda Siriwardana and Lakshan Sandakan did not bowl that well and it let them down. Does not see any reason to panic and ensures that his side will fare better in the next game. On Chandimal's fitness, he hopes that his vice captain will be fit for the second ODI.

MAN OF THE MATCH, JAMES FAULKNER is really happy as this was his very first performance in Sri Lanka. Adds the wicket wasn't easy to bat on. Further says he kept on changing his pace and got the reward for the same. Adds the Australian fielders were outstanding as they grabbed everything that came their way.

Not a bad game for Sri Lanka, they almost managed to snatch a win from defeat. Dilruwan Perera finished with 3 wickets while the debutant Aponso was excellent for figures of 10-1-27-1. Perhaps, had they scored 20-30 runs more, they might have won the game.

At 190/3, OZ were well in the hunt, needing just 38 to win from 74 balls. However, a couple of quick wickets put them in trouble and in the end, they managed to just scrape through. Experience shows what it can do as it was the innings of 56 by Finch at the top which set the platform and the 58 by Smith which ensured there was no collapse in the middle. There were good supporting knocks, mainly from Wade(26) who shifted the pressure thanks to a quick knock while Bailey's 39 was like how a child feels secured with its parents. It gave an assurance to the dressing room.

On a track which was turning square, chasing 228 was never going to be easy. And Sri Lanka did not make life easy either. Of the 46.5 overs bowled, only 12 were delivered by the pacers. Australia got off to a rollicking start but soon, Warner was on his way after a sluggish innings. However, the visitors kept building meaningful partnerships and were in control for three quarters of the game. However, there was a surprise in store.

Finally a win for Australia in an international game in the Isles of Sri Lanka on this tough tour. They were whitewashed in the Test series 0-3 and almost managed to lose this one after securing it in the bag. However, in the end, their experience helped them to get the better of their nerves.

THAT'S IT! AUSTRALIA WIN BY 3 WICKETS WITH 17 BALLS TO SPARE! Smith is a happy man and the Australian dressing room erupts in joy, what a moment this is for them as they have registered their highest successful run chase in ODIs in Sri Lanka. Back of a length outside off, watchfully punched away.
Landed outside off, watchfully defended.
Captain STEVEN SMITH walks in at number 3, replacing Warner.

OUT! Thisara gets the breakthrough! Sometimes, they say, one should not swerve from one's basic instincts. David Warner is usually an attacking batsman but tonight he was playing second fiddle with Finch being the aggressor. That seems to have gone against him, as Warner was not looking his own self. Pitched on a fuller length around middle, moving away. That squares Warner up. He pushes at it and gets a thick outside edge which dips low on its way to the keeper. But Kusal Perera dives forward and takes it with both hands. Thisara appeals but Warner does not even bother to wait for the umpire's call. Off he goes. AUSTRALIA NEED 188 FROM 256 BALLS.
Landed on middle and leg, defended from the crease.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a run.

Excellent fielding. Short and outside off, Aaron punches it through the covers where Siriwardana dives to his right at cover-point and keeps the batsmen to just a single. That was a boundary had it gone through. 189 more needed from 249 balls.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
On middle, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
Very straight again, defended watchfully.
Full and straight, pushed defensively towards mid on.
Thisara was ready to bowl the 7th ball of this over but the umpire intervened at the last moment.
FOUR! This time he puts it away! A length ball down the leg side, Finch just tucks it away past short fine leg and gets a boundary!
Down the leg side, Finch looks to tuck it away but misses. No wide signalled from the umpire. Finch has missed out there, with fine leg inside the circle.
Short and outside off, punched straight to short extra cover.
Outside off, defended watchfully.
Outside off, dabbed to third man for a single.

EXCELLENT EFFORT! He might be nearing 40, but he is showing reflexes that of a 20-year old. Superb from Dilshan. It is a short ball outside off from Thisara, a gentle loosener, but Warner is not at all gentle on it. He crunches this through point but that old warhorse, Tillakaratne Dilshan, throws himself to his left and stops the ball, that too, cleanly. Take a bow.
THISARA PERERA is introduced into the attack.

A lovely ball, keeps it on a length just outside off, makes it to nip back in, AF looks to defend but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads. The ball rolls towards point and Finch wants the single but is sent back. A good over from Mathews.
Full on middle, worked straight to short mid-wicket.

Slightly short of a length outside off, cut behind point where Tillakaratne Dilshan dives to his right and gets a hand to it, but makes a partial stop. The ball goes through to deep backward point and the batsmen take a single.
Tight consistent line from the skipper, no room to David who blocks this one safely.
Full on middle, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
Full and straight, cannot do much with that if you are a batsman, so Warner defends.

On middle and leg, flicked through square leg. Hmmm... not much rotation of strike from the Aussies thus far. Will get difficult for them later on if they just keep blocking or go for big hits. 10 from the over.
Full and just outside off, this is watchfully defended.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket.
FOUR! He goes again! Full on middle, Finch gets down once more and mows it over mid-wicket through another slog sweep. 197 more needed from 279 balls now.
Full on middle and leg, flicked straight to square leg.
SIX! Bang! Full on middle, Finch gets down and slog sweeps this over mid-wicket for a biggie! That was a mighty hit!
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Short and outside off, cut through point where Dilshan dives to his right to stop that.
Short and outside off again, punched wide of mid off for a quick single.

Short and outside off, Finch looks to cut but there is some extra bounce and he misses. Kusal Perera struggles to adjust as well and the ball bursts through. Two runs taken, byes signalled. 208 more needed from 285 balls.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
On a good length around off, nipping back in, defended from the crease.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Fullish on middle and leg, AF sweeps it straight to short fine leg.
FOUR! Audacious! A long hop on middle, Finch goes back and drags it via a pull shot over mid-wicket and gets a boundary!

EDGED! DROPPED! Tough chance. Short and outside off, Warner looks to cut but the ball comes in with the angle, takes the inside edge and goes to the keeper. However, Kusal Perera is unable to hang on. He had taken a similar catch in the third Test. A single taken.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
Full on middle and leg, worked through square leg for a single.
TILLAKARATNE DILSHAN to bowl with the second new ball.
This one nips back in and stays low, AF works it wide of mid on for a quick single.
WIDE. Unlucky for the bowler. Slants this down the leg side, Finch looks to tuck it away but misses. The keeper fumbles and the umpire signals a wide but replays show that it came off the pad.
On a good length just outside off, that is the spot, Aaron comes forward to defend but the ball kicks off the surface and hits him on the glove and goes to point.
This one nips back in, Finch is watchful in defense.
SIX! What a shot. Full and outside off, Finch plays this with a straight bat and lofts this cleanly over the bowler and it lands just in front of the sight screen! 219 more needed from 297 balls.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Short and outside off, Warner punches it through the covers. The ball is stopped near the ropes and the batsmen take three.
Welcome back. 228 needed for the Aussies to go 1-0 up. Looks difficult. Out come WARNER and FINCH. Angelo Mathews to start off proceedings to Warner. Here we go...
